title: Define per-frame animation/skinning performance budget and benchmark
description:
## Summary
Define and guard an explicit RUNTIME per-frame performance budget for the animated/skinned path (pose + Unity skinning), because the MVP treats performance as first-class and no per-frame budget is documented anywhere. Generation-time budgets (TSK-0008/TSK-0119) are a different pipeline phase and must not be conflated.

## User Mandate
STRICT: Round 5, sequential review in D:\UnityProjects\CreatureCreator. Owning task TSK-0134 Define per-frame animation/skinning performance budget and benchmark. Do not commit or push. Review the current task record, existing GenerateDataBenchmark/performance harnesses, and any uncommitted benchmark-related changes. Read Assets/Scripts/README.md and the full TSK-0134 task.

Acceptance: define and measure separate steady-state animation/skinning and geometry-rebind budgets; report allocations and scaling data with exact workload/repetition details; distinguish hot-path pose application from rebind/generation; do not claim Unity performance evidence from source inspection or .NET builds. Preserve indexed pose application and avoid speculative benchmark framework duplication. Falsifiable hypothesis: an existing harness can be extended minimally to capture both budgets without changing runtime behavior. Discriminator: inventory current harnesses and run the narrowest available benchmark/test gate; if Unity/profiling is unavailable, make only the smallest evidence/documentation change justified by the task and record the blocker rather than inventing numbers. Do not touch extraction, skeleton contracts, bridge tests, or GeneratedCreature code.

Required report: changed files, exact commands/results, Unity version/test mode, measurements if any, non-obvious decisions, blockers, residual risk, and next step.

## Scope
- State a concrete target: e.g., a per-creature per-frame ceiling for `ApplyPose` + `SkinnedMeshRenderer` deformation at a target bone/vertex count and creature count at 60fps.
- Add a benchmark harness measuring the SMR/adapter end-to-end frame cost on a REAL generated creature (mirrors TSK-0008's methodology but for the runtime frame, not generation time).
- Anchor on TSK-0118's 0.555ms/1000-calls, 0-bytes `ApplyPose` data point, but scope to the NEW per-vertex skinning + renderer cost this MVP adds (do not re-benchmark what 0118 already closed).
- Record at least: animation tick CPU, ApplyPose CPU, managed allocations/frame, renderer count, bone count, vertex count, influence count; test small/medium/high-bone-count creatures.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A documented per-frame budget number exists for the animated path.
- The benchmark runs in PlayMode on real generated geometry and records managed allocations (target 0 after warmup) and elapsed under budget.
- Regression gate: no per-frame SDF regen, mesh rebuild, weight recalculation, semantic/string resolution, or CPU LinearBlendSkinning in the walking/idle frame loop.

## Validation
PLAY MODE REQUIRED for the authoritative SMR/adapter frame cost. Runs LAST (there is no SMR frame to measure until 0132/0133 land). dotnet builds + git diff --check.

## Findings
Confirmed (source + docs): every existing performance figure (TSK-0008 ~147ms FieldSampling baseline, B0) is generation-time, once-per-edit. No per-frame benchmark/budget exists for a posed SkinnedMeshRenderer. TSK-0118's 0.555ms/1000-calls, 0-bytes measured bone posing only, not the new per-vertex skinning cost.

## Blockers
Depends on 0132 (adapter) and 0133 (driver) to have a frame to measure; Unity required to close.

## Next Step
Formalize the budget + benchmark after 0132/0133 land; embed a minimal zero-alloc ceiling as an acceptance criterion of 0132 in the meantime so performance stays first-class during the adapter build. Preserve the two-budget split from the 2026-09-07 audit disposition: (A) steady-state pose tick, ApplyPose, enabled SkinnedMeshRenderer deformation, and per-frame allocations; (B) geometry rebind latency and allocations for implicit-surface weight authoring plus skinning-mesh copying after live geometry replacement.

## Audit synthesis disposition (2026-09-07)

The follow-up audits confirm this task is still the correct owner, but its scope must cover two distinct budgets before execution: (A) steady-state pose tick, ApplyPose, Unity SkinnedMeshRenderer/GPU deformation, and per-frame allocations; (B) rebind latency and allocations for implicit-surface weight authoring plus skinning-mesh copying after live geometry replacement. Do not merge these into one number.

No profiler result is available in this reconciliation. The bind-time concern is source-confirmed algorithmic complexity, not a measured regression: implicit weight authoring scans vertices against eligible segments and CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer copies source mesh arrays during bind. Keep status Backlog until the benchmark is implemented and Unity PlayMode evidence exists. Evidence: both supplied animation audits and direct source verification.

## Round 5 review evidence (2026-09-07)

### Inventory and hypothesis check
The falsifiable hypothesis was that an existing harness could be extended minimally to measure both budgets without runtime changes. The discriminator does not support that conclusion yet: `Assets/Scripts/Tests/Runtime/GenerateDataBenchmark.cs` is explicitly an opt-in TSK-0135/TSK-0008 generation benchmark. It reports VPU 10 and 16, 7 timed repetitions plus 1 discarded warmup, generation stage timings, and managed-heap deltas only; it does not exercise animation, an enabled `SkinnedMeshRenderer`, or rebind.

Existing runtime tests provide a narrow pose check but not the TSK-0134 acceptance gate:
- `CreatureRigTests.ApplyPose_RepeatedCallsAllocateNoManagedMemoryAfterWarmup`: 16 warmup calls, then 1,000 indexed `ApplyPose` calls; asserts 0 managed bytes and logs elapsed milliseconds.
- `CreatureSkinnedMeshRendererTests.PerFrame_ApplyPose_AllocatesNoManagedMemory_AndDoesNotRebuildMesh`: 8 warmup calls, then 1,000 indexed `ApplyPose` calls; asserts 0 managed bytes, stable shared mesh, stable bone-weight count, and stable bindpose count.
- The latter does not measure enabled renderer deformation/GPU cost, animation tick cost, scaling across small/medium/high bone and vertex counts, or bind/rebind latency/allocations.

The owning runtime split is already correct: `CreatureRig.ApplyPose` owns the indexed hot path; `CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer.Bind` owns one-time weight authoring, bindpose/bone-weight construction, mesh copying, and replacement cleanup. No runtime behavior was changed and no second benchmark framework was added.

### Exact gates
- `dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Runtime.csproj --no-restore`: passed, exit 0.
- `dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime.csproj --no-restore`: passed, exit 0.
- `dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Editor.csproj --no-restore`: passed, exit 0.
- `dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Tests.Editor.csproj --no-restore`: passed, exit 0.
- `git status --short -- Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Animation Assets/Scripts/Tests/Runtime/GenerateDataBenchmark.cs`: passed, no scoped changes.
- `git diff --check`: not clean, exit 2 because of pre-existing trailing whitespace in `Assets/Test.unity`; this is outside TSK-0134 and was not modified.

### Unity evidence
No Unity executable was found in the standard installation locations checked. Therefore no PlayMode benchmark, profiler capture, renderer/GPU measurement, allocation scaling data, or authoritative Unity test result was produced. Repository validation documentation identifies Unity `6000.0.35f1`; test mode for this review is N/A because Unity was unavailable. The .NET builds above are compilation evidence only, not performance evidence.

### Decision, blockers, residual risk
Do not define measured numeric budgets or add a speculative harness in this round. Keep TSK-0134 Backlog. The next implementation should extend the existing opt-in benchmark pattern or add one focused TSK-0134 harness only after Unity is available, with separate workloads/repetitions for: (A) steady-state enabled SMR pose/deformation and (B) geometry rebind after replacement. It must report exact renderer/bone/vertex/influence counts, animation tick and `ApplyPose` timing, managed allocations after warmup, rebind timing/allocations, and small/medium/high scaling. Residual risk: existing tests establish zero managed allocation for indexed pose application and no mesh rebuild, but do not establish the enabled renderer/GPU frame budget or rebind budget.

## Audit synthesis disposition (2026-09-10)
Keep this task open as the sole performance evidence owner. Absorb F-11's per-solve `Dictionary<string, Vector3>` allocation only after measurement, and F-12's missing bind/rebind budget for implicit weight authoring and mesh-array copying. Separate steady-state pose/skinning budget from generation/rebind budget; require Unity PlayMode/profiler evidence.
